newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTR$-Placer Dome says to issue pref shares.
newsitem.headline: RTR$-Placer Dome says to issue pref shares.

text.p: Placer Dome Inc chief executive officer John Willson said on Thursday the company planned to issue preference shares to finance its takeover bid for Highlands Gold Ltd.
However, he said the company had no plans to make a bid for Kidston Gold Mines Ltd, in which Placer Pacific holds a 70 percent stake.
"On completion of the Highlands acquisition we plan to issue preference shares to finance that transaction," Willson told reporters at a briefing.
On Kidston, he said: "We plan to keep it the way Placer Pacific has always seen it," he said.
Willson said Placer Dome had no plans yet on whether to keep, sell or swap Highlands' non-gold assets.
Highlands has been pursuing the Frieda River copper/gold project and the Ramu nickel/cobalt project, both of which are situated in Papua New Guinea.
Willson said Placer Dome was not interested in furthering its interests in PNG through the Lihir gold project.
"We have had plenty of opportunity to become involved in Lihir, but it didn't interest us," Willson said.

Willson and Placer Dome chief financial officer Ian Austin would not comment on how much Placer Dome planned to raise from the issue. The Canadian miner is offering 75 cents per Highlands share, which values the PNG miner at about A$425 million.
In regards to Highlands non-gold assets, Willson said: "We don't know much about them or what we are going to do with them, to develop them, sell them, or swap them."
Willson said he expected Placer Dome's future revenue to comprise 75 percent gold and 25 percent non-gold, which would mainly come from copper operations.
Asked further about Placer Dome's intention with Highlands' Ramu nickel/cobalt project in PNG, Willson replied; "It certainly doesn't fit our biscuit."
He said Placer Dome plans to keep its Australian sharemarket listing when the takeover offers are completed.
The Vancouver-based miner is offering one of its shares for every 15 Placer Pacific shares for the remaining 24.6 percent it does not own in its Australian offshoot.
Highlands has said the Placer Dome offer is inadequate, while Placer Pacific shareholders have advised its shareholders to take no action.
At 3.40 p.m. (0440 GMT), Highlands shares were 17 cents up at 75 cents, while Placer Pacific shares were 42 cents or 29.37 percent higher at A$1.85.
